title: The symmetric algebra of a module and its universal property
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-module. Let $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ be the quotient of the tensor algebra $\mathrm T_R(M)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}M^{\otimes n}$ by the two-sided ideal generated by the elements $x\otimes y-y\otimes x$ ($x,y\in M$), and $\iota_M:M\to\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ the $R$-linear map induced by $M=\mathrm T^1_R(M)\subseteq\mathrm T_R(M)$. Then $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ is a commutative $R$-algebra, and for every commutative $R$-algebra $B$ and every $R$-linear map $f:M\to B$ there is exactly one $R$-algebra homomorphism $\tilde f:\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)\to B$ with $\tilde f\circ\iota_M=f$. In particular two $R$-algebra homomorphisms $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)\to B$ which agree on $\iota_M(M)$ are equal.
